requirement_title: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly
requirement_text:
# REQ-2129: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2129
Type: feature

## Requirement

Given Project A (contains `ProjectA.MyType`, has no and cannot have a reference to the MessagePack NuGet package) and Project B (references Project A and MessagePack), the reporter needs a source-generated `IMessagePackFormatter` for `ProjectA.MyType` generated inside Project B.

Proposed solution: add a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute that works for partial classes implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`:

```csharp
[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]
partial class MyObjectFormatter: IMessagePackFormatter<MyObject>;
```

The class does not need a body; the implementation is source-generated by `MessagePack.SourceGenerator.MessagePackGenerator` as usual.

For attribute-based property keys and other settings (such as Union), the issue lists three alternatives: (1) use `System.Runtime.Serialization.DataMember` and related attributes; (2) let the generator and analyzers work with user-defined copies of the MessagePack attributes; (3) source-generate the attributes themselves via `RegisterPostInitializationOutput`.

Motivation: Project A is a NuGet library that should stay minimal with zero dependencies.

## Acceptance criteria

- A `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute exists and can be applied to a partial class implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`.
- The source generator emits the formatter implementation for `T` inside the annotated class, in the assembly that declares the class (Project B), even when `T` is declared in a referenced assembly.
- The annotated class may be declared without a body (`partial class X : IMessagePackFormatter<T>;`).
- `T` needs no MessagePack attributes: without `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` on `T` the generated formatter uses contractless behaviour over public members. (derived from maintainer comment)
- If `T` does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Private members are not required to be serialized; only public members are in scope. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Project A needs no reference to the MessagePack package. (derived)

## Notes from discussion

- AArnott: "We might simplistically say this only works in 'contractless' mode, such that you need no attributes on it at all. If there are attributes on it, fine, we'll use them. But if there is no `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` attribute on the type, go contractless by default."
- AArnott on prerequisite: "Does ProjectA.MyType requires only `public` members to be serialized? That seems a prerequisite for anything here." Reporter: yes.
- AArnott is not a fan of a `PropertyKeys` dictionary on the formatter, and warns that copying attributes into Project A breaks reflection-based (dynamic resolver) mode.
- AArnott suggested a surrogate-type design: `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter(SurrogateType = typeof(ProjectASurrogate))]`, keys mapped by property name; reporter: "Looks good." No design was settled in the thread.

findings.claim: The acceptance criterion 'If T does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured' is not met. `Collect` never looks at attributes on T. Without a surrogate it always calls `CreateContractlessMembers`, which takes every public read-write member, uses its name as a string key, and sorts ordinally. As a result, `[MessagePackObject]` with `[Key(int)]` keys is ignored and the wire format changes from an array to a map. `[IgnoreMember]` members are serialized. `[DataContract]`/`[DataMember]` membership and names are ignored, so non-`[DataMember]` public members are serialized. The maintainer note only allows contractless mode when T has no `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]`.

receipt_plan.detail: Run tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests/Receipts/GeneratedFormatterHonoursTypeAttributesTests.cs. Both IgnoreMemberOnReferencedType_IsNotSerialized and DataContractOnReferencedType_LimitsMembers fail on head because the generated `partial class MyTypeFormatter` source references IgnoredSecretValue / NotADataMember.

findings.claim: The patch removes a security guard that the requirement does not touch. `MessagePackSecurity.GetHashCollisionResistantEqualityComparer<T>` used to throw `TypeAccessException` for any key type without a known hash-collision-resistant comparer. It now silently returns `EqualityComparer<T>.Default`. Under `MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData`, deserializing a dictionary or hash set keyed by an arbitrary user type is therefore accepted with a non-resistant comparer, which re-opens hash-flooding DoS. This contradicts the secure-by-default history recorded in L12.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.UntrustedDataComparerGuardTests.UntrustedDataRejectsUnknownKeyType. It calls `MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData.GetEqualityComparer<CustomKey>()` and expects `TypeAccessException`. It passes on base and fails on head.

findings.claim: `GeneratedFormatterCollector` never reads any attribute on the formatted type T. In contractless mode it serializes every public read-write member by name and ignores `[MessagePackObject]`, `[Key]`, `[IgnoreMember]`, `[DataContract]` and `[DataMember]` on T. The acceptance criterion 'If T does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured' is therefore not met. A member marked `[IgnoreMember]` on T is still serialized, and int keys are replaced by name keys, which changes the wire format.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterHonoursAttributesTests.IgnoreMemberOnFormattedTypeIsHonoured. It generates `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` for a `[MessagePackObject]` type that has an `[IgnoreMember] IgnoredSecret` property, and asserts that the generated user formatter never references `IgnoredSecret`.

hunches.claim: Out-of-scope change creates a security hole. `MessagePackSecurity.GetEqualityComparer<T>` used to throw `TypeAccessException` for types that have no hash-collision-resistant comparer. It now silently returns `EqualityComparer<T>.Default`. Under `MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData`, deserializing a dictionary or hash set keyed by an arbitrary type therefore uses a non-resistant comparer, which re-opens the hash-flooding DoS that this guard closed. REQ-2129 asks for nothing in this area, and the change contradicts the secure-by-default history recorded in L12.

receipt_plan.detail: In MessagePack.Tests, add `[Fact] public void UntrustedData_UnknownKeyType_Throws() => Assert.Throws<TypeAccessException>(() => MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData.GetEqualityComparer<SomeUserClass>());` using a plain user class. It passes on base and fails on head because no exception is thrown.

hunches.claim: GetEqualityComparer's fallback for unknown types now returns EqualityComparer<T>.Default instead of throwing TypeAccessException. In untrusted-data mode, types that were rejected as not hash-resistant are now silently accepted as keys in hash collections, which reintroduces the hash-collision DoS vector. It is also a behavioral change for existing users, and the requirement does not ask for it.

receipt_plan.detail: With MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData, deserialize a Dictionary<CustomKeyType,int> where CustomKeyType has no registered hash-resistant comparer. Base throws TypeAccessException; head succeeds. Assert that it throws.

hunches.claim: The ForAttributeWithMetadataName transform returns new GeneratedFormatterRequest holding raw INamedTypeSymbol values, and the pipeline then combines it with the compilation. Each compilation change therefore regenerates all output. The extra Combine also changes the s.Left.* tuple shape. A pipeline-shape change like this is a regression risk for the generated output, so the snapshot tests should be rerun.

receipt_plan.detail: Rerun the existing generator snapshot tests for ordinary [MessagePackObject] types and confirm the generated output is byte-identical to base.

hunches.claim: The contractless mode orders members by ordinal name and assigns int keys 0..n-1. Members are only public read-write ones, so read-only properties and fields are dropped. The wire format for contractless types is therefore not the same as the dynamic contractless resolver. Pre-existing hand-written or reflection formatters for the same type will produce different bytes (string-key maps compared with the dynamic resolver's ordering and read-only handling).

receipt_plan.detail: Serialize a type with public get-only property, get/set property, and field using ContractlessStandardResolver versus the generated formatter. Compare the bytes for member presence and order.

hunches.claim: The user-declared formatter's generated partial class is emitted without the partial class's accessibility or generic constraints being aligned. The generated partial 'partial class Name : IMessagePackFormatter<T>' re-declares the interface. This is fine, but the same formatter is also registered in the resolver via ObjectSerializationInfo. The resolver may therefore reference the user's class as 'new Formatter()'. If that class has no public parameterless constructor or is private/nested, the generated resolver code will not compile in user projects.

receipt_plan.detail: Generate output for a private nested [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] class and one with a parameterized constructor. Compile the generated resolver and check for errors.

hunches.claim: GetEqualityComparer<T>() previously threw TypeAccessException for any type with no known hash-resistant comparer, which is how MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData protects against hash-collision DoS. It now returns EqualityComparer<T>.Default. Deserializing attacker-controlled keys into Dictionary/HashSet with an arbitrary key type under UntrustedData is therefore silently allowed with a non-resistant comparer. This removes the protection, and nothing in REQ-2129 calls for it.

receipt_plan.detail: Deserialize a Dictionary<CustomKeyType,int> (CustomKeyType has a weak GetHashCode) with MessagePackSerializerOptions.Standard.WithSecurity(MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData). Base build throws TypeAccessException ("No hash-resistant equality comparer available"); head build succeeds. The existing MessagePackSecurityTests case that expects TypeAccessException for an unsupported key type should fail on head.

hunches.claim: MessagePackSecurity.GetHashCollisionResistantEqualityComparer fallback was changed from throwing TypeAccessException to returning EqualityComparer<T>.Default. This silently removes the hash-collision protection for untrusted data on unknown key types. It is unrelated to the feature, and the ledger records secure-by-default as a deliberate direction.

receipt_plan.detail: Deserialize a Dictionary<CustomKeyType,int> with MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData. Base throws TypeAccessException, head returns a default comparer. Run the existing MessagePackSecurityTests. Also cite [L12].

hunches.claim: Acceptance says that if T carries MessagePack attributes they are honoured. The collector ignores [MessagePackObject], [Key], [DataContract] and [IgnoreMember] on T itself. It always uses contractless mode unless a surrogate is given.

receipt_plan.detail: Generate a formatter for a same-compilation type with [MessagePackObject] and [Key(0)] members. Assert the output is an int-key array, not a string-key map.

hunches.claim: The change replaces the TypeAccessException in the hash-resistant comparer fallback with EqualityComparer<T>.Default. This silently removes a security guard, and no test touches it or would fail if the line were reverted. It is unrelated to REQ-2129.

The surrogate negative cases cover only a missing member and a type mismatch, so the IsPublicReadWrite check on the target is untested.

hunches.claim: The GeneratorUtilities filter that excludes [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] classes from hand-written formatter registration is only indirectly tested. The registration test asserts the resolver returns the right type, but a duplicate registration might still compile or be tolerated. There are no generator snapshot tests for the emitted code.

receipt_plan.detail: GeneratorUtilities.cs:38 remove-guard: delete the `!symbol.GetAttributes().Any(...)` condition; may survive or fail to compile only incidentally, with no explicit test

hunches.claim: The requirement says contractless behaviour over public members, but the generated formatter covers less than MessagePack's existing contractless mode. `IsPublicReadWrite` drops every get-only or init-less public property, so these members are silently not serialized at all, even on the serialize side. In addition, a class whose only constructor takes parameters (for example a positional record, common in dependency-free libraries) is rejected with MsgPack007 instead of matching constructor parameters by name as `ContractlessStandardResolver` does. Immutable public types from Project A therefore lose data or get no formatter.

receipt_plan.detail: In GeneratedFormatterCollector.cs, `CreateContractlessMembers` filters with `IsPublicReadWrite`, which requires a public setter (lines 135 and 275-282). The isClass check at line 77 returns null with `NoDeserializingConstructor` when there is no parameterless ctor, and `constructorParameters` is always empty. Compare with DynamicContractlessObjectResolver, which serializes get-only public properties and binds ctor parameters.

hunches.claim: When T is a `[MessagePackObject]` declared in the same compilation, two formatters are produced for it. `TypeCollector` still collects T and emits its own formatter, and `GeneratedFormatterCollector` adds a second `ObjectSerializationInfo` for the same data type. Nothing deduplicates by data type, so the resolver may register two formatters for T, or pick one arbitrarily.

receipt_plan.detail: Read the foreach over `s.Left.Left.Right`: it calls `modelPerType.Add(generatedModel)` with no check that `info.DataType` was already collected from `messagePackObjectTypes`. Then inspect the generated resolver source for duplicate entries for MyObject.

hunches.claim: `IsPartial` checks only the formatter class's own modifiers. For a formatter nested in a non-partial outer class (`class Outer { [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial class F : IMessagePackFormatter<T> {} }`), the template's `EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces` re-declares `Outer` as partial. The generated code then fails to compile with a CS0260-style error, and no MsgPack019 diagnostic is reported.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the generator on a nested formatter inside a non-partial outer class. Expect a compiler error on the generated file instead of a MsgPack019 diagnostic.

hunches.claim: `IsPublicReadWrite` checks `property.SetMethod` on the most-derived declaration only, because `GetInstanceMembers` keeps just the most derived member of each name. If a derived type overrides a read-write property but declares only `get`, Roslyn returns a null `SetMethod` for that override. The property is then silently dropped in contractless mode, and in surrogate mode it is reported as MsgPack022.

receipt_plan.detail: Use a base class with `public virtual int X { get; set; }` and a derived class with `public override int X => 1;`. Generate a formatter for the derived type and observe that X is absent from the generated members.

hunches.claim: Formatters declared as `partial record` are silently ignored. The generator predicate accepts only `ClassDeclarationSyntax`, and `IsPartial` uses `OfType<ClassDeclarationSyntax>`. A `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial record F : IMessagePackFormatter<T>` therefore gets no generated body and no diagnostic.

receipt_plan.detail: Apply the attribute to a partial record class (LanguageVersion latest). Observe that no source is generated and no MsgPack019/020 diagnostic is reported; only CS0535 appears.

hunches.claim: The generated-formatter diagnostics MsgPack019-022 are registered in the analyzer SupportedDiagnostics but are not added to AnalyzerReleases.Unshipped.md. There are also no doc/analyzers pages, even though the helpLinkUri points to them. Under the RS2000 release-tracking check this breaks the analyzer build. The generator collector also reuses MsgPack004/NoDeserializingConstructor diagnostics outside their original context.

receipt_plan.detail: Compare the AnalyzerReleases.Unshipped.md entries with the new IDs MsgPack019-022. Check that doc/analyzers/MsgPack019.md through MsgPack022.md exist.

hunches.claim: The new analyzer diagnostics MsgPack019-022 are reported only from the generator, but SupportedDiagnostics in the analyzer lists them. The analyzer itself never reports them. This is inconsistent with the other MsgPack00x rules, which are analyzer-driven.

receipt_plan.detail: MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer registers no action for GeneratedMessagePackFormatter. Diagnostics come from the generator's RegisterSourceOutput.

hunches.claim: suppressed by unconfirmed context entry: [L11] area=analyzer, generator: Types that come from a referenced assembly are deliberately not analysed and get no formatter from the compiling assembly. In `TypeCollector.CollectCore`, after the custom-formatter, enum and generic checks, a non-generic type whose symbol is metadata-only exits with a bare `if (type.Locations[0].IsInMetadata) { return; }` (TypeCollector.cs:367-370), so no MsgPack003/004/005 diagnostic and no generated formatter appear for it. The defining assembly owns validating and formatting its own types (rationale inferred: the code has no comment). A missing diagnostic or formatter for such a type is not a defect. (source: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:367) (would-be finding: The generator never analyses types from referenced assemblies and creates no formatter for them ([L11]). The change deliberately bypasses that by generating formatters for metadata-only types through GeneratedFormatterCollector. This is an opt-in explicit attribute path, so it is consistent with the ledger.)

receipt_plan.detail: [L11] TypeCollector.CollectCore returns early for metadata-only types. The new path is separate, opt-in via [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter], and does not alter that check.

hunches.claim: suppressed by unconfirmed context entry: [L8] area=docs: Requiring the MessagePackObject annotation by default is intentional, to enforce explicitness. (source: README.md); [L3] area=annotations: Serializable types must be public by default and need [MessagePackObject], and keyAsPropertyName: true makes members use their property names as string keys without [Key]. (source: README.md) (would-be finding: Contractless mode without [MessagePackObject] contradicts the default of requiring annotations. The ledger says that requirement is intentional, for explicitness. It applies here only through the explicit attribute, which is consistent with the requirement's maintainer comment.)

receipt_plan.detail: [L8]/[L3] annotation required by default. Here the explicit [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] opt-in supplies the explicitness, and the requirement's derived criteria allow contractless.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Add [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] with an optional SurrogateType property, where a user-defined surrogate type in Project B mirrors T's shape and keys are mapped by property name, so attribute-based keys and Union settings can be supplied without touching Project A. Code: Attribute has a SurrogateType property; generator reads keys/union attributes from the surrogate and emits conversion code between T and the surrogate, which the contractless-only reading would not do.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Add [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] for a partial class implementing IMessagePackFormatter<T>, generating a contractless formatter over T's public members (honouring any MessagePack attributes present) in the declaring assembly, with no surrogate type. Code: Generator discovers classes with the attribute, reads T from the IMessagePackFormatter<T> interface, and emits Serialize/Deserialize directly for T's public members, defaulting to contractless when T has no [MessagePackObject]/[DataContract]; no SurrogateType property.
